title: A DeepSharp pipeline
description: The steps of a pipeline in the order they were written, and what the fit learned from the training rows.

version.description: The version of the pipeline file this was written against; the first, when it is left out.

declaration.description: The steps, in the order they run.

step.description: One step of the pipeline, named by its verb.

fitted.description: What each step learned from the training rows, written by the fit rather than by a person: an entry for each step that learned something, filed under the key of the steps it learned behind.

prefix.description: The key of the steps up to the one that learned this: a SHA-256 digest, in hexadecimal.

skipped.description: The steps a run for a learner left out, written by the run rather than by a person: an entry for each, filed under the key of the steps up to it; written only when a run left one out.

prefix.description: The key of the steps up to the one left out: a SHA-256 digest, in hexadecimal.

declare.description: Names the columns that take part, says what each holds, and decides what becomes of the rest.

remainder.description: What becomes of the columns the schema does not name: dropped, kept as text, or refused.

columns.description: The columns that take part, what each holds, and whether the source may lack it.

name.description: The column's name in the source.

optional.description: Whether the source is allowed not to have the column at all.

excluded.description: Whether the column is left out while its kind is kept, so it can be taken in again as it was. Left out, the column takes part.

was.description: The kind a category column held before it was made one, so it can go back to it. Left out, there is none.

format.description: How a timestamp column's moments are written, as .NET writes a date format: dd/MM/yyyy, say. Left out, they are read as ISO 8601 writes them.

missing.description: A value that stands for a gap in the column, read as the gap it is: 0, say, where a file writes 0 for a fare nobody knows. Left out, none does.

id.description: Whether the column names each row: carried with the rows, as read, and never a feature. Left out, it does not.

drop.columns.description: Leaves columns out from here on.

columns.description: The columns to leave out from here on.

drop.gaps.description: Drops every row that has a gap in any of the named columns, before the rows are divided.

columns.description: The columns a row may not have a gap in.

drop.warmup.description: Drops the rows at the start that an indicator cannot yet speak for.

atMost.description: The most rows this may drop from the start; beyond it the run stops rather than shrink the data to nothing.

encode.description: Writes a column of words down as numbers, using the categories the training rows held.

column.description: The column of words to write down as numbers.

as.description: How the categories are written down: one column per category, or one column of places.

unseen.description: What happens to a category the training rows never held: a place kept for it, or a refusal.

encode.categories.description: Writes every column that stands for a group down as numbers, each by the categories the training rows held.

as.description: How each category is written down: one column per category, or one column of places.

unseen.description: What happens to a category the training rows never held: a place kept for it, or a refusal.

encode.piecewise.description: Writes a column of numbers down as how far each value fills a few bins, their edges the training rows' quantiles.

column.description: The column of numbers to write down as bins.

bins.description: How many bins the training rows' quantiles divide the values into, at least two; fewer where edges fall together.

outOfRange.description: What happens to a value beyond the edges the training rows set: let through the end bins, held at them, or refused.

evidence.correlation.description: Sets out the rows a correlation between columns is drawn from, on the rows the split trains on, and how many it kept.

columns.description: The columns to correlate with one another: two or more, each holding numbers.

shown.description: How it is shown: drawn as a coloured grid, or as the numbers themselves.

coefficient.description: Which coefficient is shown: how well two columns lie on a line (pearson), or how well they keep the same order (spearman). Left out, pearson.

evidence.likeness.description: Sets out how alike the parts a split made are, column by column, and flags the ones further apart than a bound.

warnAbove.description: The distance above which two parts are flagged as unlike: a share above nought, at most one.

columns.description: The columns to compare across the parts; left out, every column where it stands but the answer.

evidence.profile.description: Profiles the columns where it stands, on the rows the split trains on, and names what is wrong or should not be there, with how each is answered.

columns.description: The columns to profile; left out, every column where the step stands.

rankAbove.description: How alike in order two columns of numbers may be before the profile says so: a share above nought, at most one. Two columns whose Spearman coefficient, on the rows where both hold a number, is above this in size are flagged. Left out, none is.

evidence.report.description: Names the measures a trained model is held to, the parts they are taken on and how they are shown, each in the answer's own units.

metrics.description: The measures, in the order they are shown: rmse, mae, r2 and mape for amounts, and the coverage and width of an interval; accuracy, precision, recall, the confusion matrix, f1, auc and brier for classes; kl for shares of a whole; emd and rps for shares in an order.

parts.description: The parts they are taken on, side by side: the rows a model learns from, the rows it is chosen on and the rows it is tested on. The rows held back to predict on, and the rows a split keeps apart, are measured on by nothing.

shown.description: How they are shown: drawn, as the numbers themselves, or both.

feature.add.description: Adds a column worked out from two others by plain arithmetic.

column.description: What the new column is called.

left.description: The column on the left of the arithmetic.

arithmetic.description: What is done with the two columns: added, subtracted, multiplied or divided.

right.description: The column on the right of the arithmetic.

feature.cycle.description: Writes a number as a place on a circle of a length you give, so that the ends of the cycle meet.

length.description: How long one turn is, in the column's own units: 7 for an age in days on a week. Said by you, never worked out from the rows.

form.description: How the two values are written down: as they are, shifted between nothing and one, or split into how far up and how far down.

feature.cyclical.description: Writes a moment in time as a place on a circle, so that the ends of a cycle meet.

column.description: The column holding the moment in time.

period.description: Which cycle the moment is placed on: the hour of the day, the day of the week, of the month or of the year, the month of the year, the season.

form.description: How the two values are written down: as they are, shifted between nothing and one, or split into how far up and how far down.

feature.indicator.description: Adds a market indicator worked out from the rows that came before: an average, a strength index, a band.

column.description: What the new column is called; an indicator with several parts adds a suffix for each.

indicator.description: Which indicator, worked out from the rows that came before.

period.description: The look-back in rows, for an indicator that takes one.

columns.description: The columns it reads, in the order the indicator expects them.

feature.timeParts.description: Takes a moment in time apart into the pieces people reason with: an hour, a weekday, a month.

column.description: The column holding the moment in time.

asCategories.description: Whether the pieces stand for a group, which they do unless the order is the point.

parts.description: Which pieces of the moment become columns of their own.

fill.missing.description: Fills the gaps in a column the named way, below the split, and marks where they were. A value no row decided is settle.gaps, above it.

column.description: The column with gaps in it.

with.description: What goes in the gaps: the mean or the median of the training rows, the value before the gap, nought, a constant, or refuse.

refuseAbove.description: The share of the training rows that may be gaps and still be filled. Above it the column is not filled, and the column that says where the gaps were speaks for it. Left out, every share is filled.

fill.nan.description: Deals with a value that is not a number a model can use; refusing it is the default.

column.description: The column to watch for values that are not numbers a model can use.

with.description: What happens to a value that is not a number: refuse, which is the default and usually the right answer, or mean, median, zero or constant.

history.description: Writes beside each row the mean of a column over the earlier training rows of its key, pulled towards the training rows' mean.

key.description: The column whose value says which rows are of one kind: a farm, a type.

value.description: The column of numbers whose mean over the earlier rows of the same kind is read.

orderBy.description: The columns that say which rows came before a row: the first decides, each next one decides between rows the ones before call equal.

shrink.description: How many rows' worth of weight the mean of every training row has beside a key's own rows, above nothing: the larger, the more a key with few rows is pulled towards it.

into.description: The name of the column it makes; left out, the value's name, 'history' and the key's name.

learn.ml.description: Names the trainer from ML.NET this pipeline is declared for: which trainer, the settings it takes and the seed it repeats from.

oneOf.description: Gradient-boosted trees: each tree corrects what the ones before it got wrong. The usual first answer for a table.

leaves.description: How many leaves one tree may grow to: the larger it is, the finer the splits and the easier it is to learn the training rows by heart.

leastRows.description: The fewest training rows a leaf may stand for, which is what keeps a split from being one passenger's story.

rate.description: How much of each tree's correction is taken: smaller is slower and steadier.

oneOf.description: A forest of trees grown apart and averaged, which holds up better on few rows than boosting does.

leaves.description: How many leaves one tree may grow to: the larger it is, the finer the splits and the easier it is to learn the training rows by heart.

leastRows.description: The fewest training rows a leaf may stand for, which is what keeps a split from being one passenger's story.

trainer.description: The trainer these rows are prepared for, and the settings it takes.

seed.description: The number the trainer's own random draws are worked out from, so the same declaration gives the same model.

learn.network.description: Names the network this pipeline is declared for: its layers, what moves them, what judges them, when the run stops and the engine it runs on.

oneOf.description: A layer that answers with as many numbers as it is given, each a weighted sum of the ones below it.

units.description: How many numbers the layer answers with.

bias.description: Whether the layer adds a bias of its own to every sum; it does, unless it says it does not.

weights.description: How the weights of the layer start; as PyTorch starts a linear layer's, unless said.

biasStart.description: How the bias of the layer starts, when it has one; as PyTorch starts it, unless said.

l1.description: How much of the sum of the absolute values of the layer's weights the loss adds, as Keras's L1 regularizer does; none, unless said.

l2.description: How much of the sum of the squares of the layer's weights the loss adds, as Keras's L2 regularizer does; none, unless said.

maxNorm.description: The most norm each unit's weights may have after a step, as Keras's MaxNorm holds them to; nought, or left out, for no bound.

learns.description: Whether the layer's numbers learn, or are held still as Keras's trainable = False holds them; they learn, unless said.

rateShare.description: The share of the run's rate the layer's numbers move at, as a learning rate of their own for a part of the network; the whole rate, unless said.

rank.description: The rank of a low-rank pair kept beside the layer's held kernel, as Keras's enable_lora keeps one; nought, or left out, for no pair.

alpha.description: What the pair's product is scaled by over the rank; nought, or left out, for the rank itself, which scales by one.

oneOf.description: Leaves what is below nought at nought.
Squashes every number between minus one and one.
Squashes every number between nought and one.
Leaves a share of the numbers out at every pass while training, and none while serving.

rate.description: The share of numbers left out at every pass while training, between nothing and one.

oneOf.description: Brings every number to the mean and spread of the rows it was trained on.

momentum.description: How much of what was measured before carries on.

epsilon.description: The small number added so nothing is divided by nought.

scale.description: Whether it multiplies what it normalised by a scale of its own; it does, unless it says it does not.

shift.description: Whether it adds a shift of its own to what it normalised; it does, unless it says it does not.

learns.description: Whether the layer's numbers learn, or are held still as Keras's trainable = False holds them; they learn, unless said.

rateShare.description: The share of the run's rate the layer's numbers move at, as a learning rate of their own for a part of the network; the whole rate, unless said.

oneOf.description: Brings every number of one row to that row's own mean and spread.

epsilon.description: The small number added so nothing is divided by nought.

scale.description: Whether it multiplies what it normalised by a scale of its own; it does, unless it says it does not.

shift.description: Whether it adds a shift of its own to what it normalised; it does, unless it says it does not.

learns.description: Whether the layer's numbers learn, or are held still as Keras's trainable = False holds them; they learn, unless said.

rateShare.description: The share of the run's rate the layer's numbers move at, as a learning rate of their own for a part of the network; the whole rate, unless said.

oneOf.description: Weighs every number by the share of a normal curve below it: smooth where relu bends.

approximate.description: Whether it is the hyperbolic tangent's approximation of the curve rather than the exact one, which PyTorch and Keras use unless told.

oneOf.description: Weighs every number by its own sigmoid; also called swish.
Weighs every number by the hyperbolic tangent of its softplus.
Leaves what is above nought, and lets a share of what is below it through.

negativeSlope.description: The share of a number below nought let through: a hundredth in PyTorch, three tenths in Keras's layer.

oneOf.description: Leaves what is above nought, and lets a share of what is below it through that it learns.

eachFeature.description: Whether every number of a row learns a share of its own, rather than one share for them all, as PyTorch starts it.

oneOf.description: Leaves what is above nought, and bends what is below it towards minus alpha.

alpha.description: What the numbers below nought bend towards, below nought.

oneOf.description: Bends as elu does, at the alpha and the scale that keep a network's numbers normalised.
Turns the numbers of a row into shares of one whole.
Divides every number of one row by the root of the mean of the row's squares, and scales it.

epsilon.description: The small number added to the mean of the squares so nothing is divided by nought; PyTorch's is the step a single-precision number takes above one.

scale.description: Whether it multiplies what it normalised by a scale of its own; it does, unless it says it does not.

learns.description: Whether the layer's numbers learn, or are held still as Keras's trainable = False holds them; they learn, unless said.

rateShare.description: The share of the run's rate the layer's numbers move at, as a learning rate of their own for a part of the network; the whole rate, unless said.

oneOf.description: Turns every number of the row into its cosines and sines at frequencies it learns, through a linear layer: a relu after it makes it PLR.

frequencies.description: How many frequencies each number is turned round at.

sigma.description: The spread of the normal curve the frequencies start from: the setting the embedding is most sensitive to, searched for every dataset by its authors, and with no default.

width.description: How many numbers each number of the row comes out as.

lite.description: Whether one linear layer is shared by every number of the row, rather than one of each number's own.

oneOf.description: Mirrors images at random while training and not while serving; it varies the rows themselves, so it stands first.

horizontal.description: Whether an image is mirrored across its columns, left for right, with a chance of a half.

vertical.description: Whether an image is mirrored across its rows, top for bottom, with a chance of a half.

seed.description: The number the variation is drawn from: its own, which the run's seed moves nothing of, and with no default.

oneOf.description: Shifts images at random while training and not while serving, padding each and cutting a window of its own size out; it stands first.

pad.description: How many places an image is padded by on every side, and so how far it can move; what moves in from outside is nought.

seed.description: The number the variation is drawn from: its own, which the run's seed moves nothing of, and with no default.

oneOf.description: Adds normal noise to every number while training and not while serving; it stands first.

spread.description: The standard deviation of the normal noise added to every number.

seed.description: The number the variation is drawn from: its own, which the run's seed moves nothing of, and with no default.

oneOf.description: Lays an example out as one row of numbers: an image as the row of its pixels.
Turns the columns a category was written down as into a small vector it learns for each category; it reads the rows as the pipeline hands them over, so it stands first.

column.description: The column of words whose categories the layer turns into vectors, as it was named before the pipeline wrote it down one column per category.

width.description: How many numbers each category's vector holds.

layers.description: The layers, from the one the prepared rows reach first.

oneOf.description: Moves every number against its gradient, carrying some of the last step's velocity.

rate.description: How far one step moves the numbers.

momentum.description: How much of the last step's velocity carries into the next.

weightDecay.description: How much of every number is added to its gradient before the step, as a share of the number itself; none, unless said.

dampening.description: How little of each new gradient the velocity takes in, from nothing to one; none, unless said.

nesterov.description: Whether the step is taken from the gradient plus the momentum times the velocity, as Nesterov has it; it is not, unless said.

oneOf.description: Moves every number by a running mean of its gradients over the root of a running mean of their squares.

rate.description: How far one step moves the numbers.

firstMoment.description: How much of the running mean of the gradients carries on.

secondMoment.description: How much of the running mean of their squares carries on.

epsilon.description: The small number added so nothing is divided by nought.

weightDecay.description: How much of every number is added to its gradient before the step, as a share of the number itself; none, unless said.

amsgrad.description: Whether the step is taken over the largest mean of the squares there has been, as AMSGrad has it; it is not, unless said.

oneOf.description: Adam, with every number shrunk towards nought before its step, apart from its gradient.

rate.description: How far one step moves the numbers.

firstMoment.description: How much of the running mean of the gradients carries on.

secondMoment.description: How much of the running mean of their squares carries on.

epsilon.description: The small number added so nothing is divided by nought.

weightDecay.description: How far every number is shrunk towards nought at each step, as a share of the step's rate.

amsgrad.description: Whether the step is taken over the largest mean of the squares there has been, as AMSGrad has it; it is not, unless said.

oneOf.description: Moves every number by its gradient over the root of a running mean of the squares of its gradients.

rate.description: How far one step moves the numbers.

alpha.description: How much of the running mean of the squares of the gradients carries on.

epsilon.description: The small number added so nothing is divided by nought.

momentum.description: How much of the last step's velocity carries into the next.

weightDecay.description: How much of every number is added to its gradient before the step, as a share of the number itself; none, unless said.

centered.description: Whether the root is taken of the mean of the squares less the square of the mean of the gradients; it is not, unless said.

oneOf.description: Adam with Nesterov's momentum, warmed up over the steps.

rate.description: How far one step moves the numbers.

firstMoment.description: How much of the running mean of the gradients carries on.

secondMoment.description: How much of the running mean of their squares carries on.

epsilon.description: The small number added so nothing is divided by nought.

momentumDecay.description: How fast the momentum warms up over the steps.

weightDecay.description: How much of every number is added to its gradient before the step, as a share of the number itself; none, unless said.

optimizer.description: What moves the network's numbers at every step.

oneOf.description: The rate the optimizer starts at, every epoch.
The rate multiplied by a factor every so many epochs.

every.description: How many epochs pass between two falls of the rate.

factor.description: What the rate is multiplied by at each fall.

oneOf.description: The rate multiplied by a factor every epoch.

factor.description: What the rate is multiplied by from one epoch to the next.

oneOf.description: The rate falling along half a cosine to its least over so many epochs.

epochs.description: How many epochs the rate falls over, along half a cosine.

minimum.description: The least rate, reached at the end of the fall.

oneOf.description: The rate rising in a straight line from a share of itself to the whole of it over so many epochs, then held.

epochs.description: How many epochs the rate warms up over.

start.description: The share of the rate the first epoch takes: above nought, and at most one.

schedule.description: How the rate changes from epoch to epoch; left out, the optimizer's own rate every epoch.

clip.description: The most norm a step's gradients may have together before they move the network; left out, or nought, they are not clipped.

clipValue.description: The most any value of a step's gradients may reach, either side of nothing, before they move the network; left out, or nought, they are not clipped by value.

stepEvery.description: How many batches' gradients are averaged into one step; left out, a step every batch.

average.description: The share an average of the network's weights keeps of itself at every step, above nothing and below one, written over the weights when the run ends; left out, or nought, none is kept.

judgedByAverage.description: Whether every epoch is judged by the average of the weights rather than by the weights as they are, so early stopping watches, and restores, the weights the run ends holding; left out, by the weights as they are.

oneOf.description: The mean of the squared differences: an answer that is an amount.
The loss of one answer among several classes, read through a softmax.

smoothing.description: How much of the answers is spread evenly before they are compared, so no label is taken as quite certain; none, unless said.

oneOf.description: The loss of an answer that is a chance, read through a sigmoid.

smoothing.description: How much of the answers is spread evenly before they are compared, so no label is taken as quite certain; none, unless said.

oneOf.description: How far the shares have to move along the order of the bands to be the answer's: an answer of shares in an order, read through a softmax.
The mean of the size of the differences: an answer that is an amount, some far off.
Half the square of the difference near the answer, its size further off: an amount with outliers.

delta.description: How far from the answer the loss stops being squared and grows in a straight line.

oneOf.description: The pinball loss: the value the answer stays below a share of the time, rather than its mean.

quantile.description: The share of the time the answer is to stay below the value the model gives: above nought and below one.

oneOf.description: A binary cross-entropy that weighs down the labels the network is already sure of: a rare class, read through a sigmoid.

gamma.description: How hard a label the network is already sure of is weighed down.

alpha.description: What a one is weighed by, and a nought by one less it — or minus one for no weight, as torchvision writes it.

oneOf.description: How far each answer falls short of a margin of one on its side of nought: a label, read by the side it falls.
The loss of a count: an answer that is how many times something happened, read through an exponential when it is a logarithm.

logInput.description: Whether the network answers with the logarithm of each count's rate, as PyTorch takes it, rather than the rate itself, as Keras does.

epsilon.description: The small number added to a rate before its logarithm is taken: a hundred-millionth in PyTorch, a ten-millionth in Keras.

loss.description: What the network's answers are judged by while it trains.

oneOf.description: The run goes on to its last pass.
The run stops once the validation loss has not fallen for as many passes as it waits.

patience.description: How many passes without a better one the run waits before it stops.

least.description: How far the validation loss has to fall below the best for a pass to count as better.

best.description: Whether the run ends holding the numbers of its best pass rather than its last.

stopping.description: When the run stops: at its last pass, or once the validation loss stops falling.

engine.description: The name of the engine the run's arithmetic happens on; which engine it stands for — and which device it works on — is the application's to say.

seed.description: The number every random draw of the run is worked out from, so the same declaration gives the same run.

epochs.description: How many times the run goes over the training rows, at most.

batch.description: How many rows one step of the run is worked out from.

maths.description: Pulls a column into another shape by arithmetic that learns nothing: a logarithm, a root, a reciprocal.

column.description: The column to pull into another shape.

maths.description: Which shape: a logarithm, a root, a reciprocal, a square, an arcsine, the magnitude or the sign.

into.description: What the result is called; the same column, unless a file says otherwise.

normalise.description: Brings a column onto a comparable scale, by numbers learned from the training rows.

column.description: The column to bring onto a comparable scale.

scale.description: Which kind of scaling: what the fit learns from the training rows.

outOfRange.description: What happens to a value outside the range the fit learned: let it through, hold it at the edge, or refuse.

normalise.row.description: Brings each row onto a comparable scale across the columns that make it up, learning nothing.

norm.description: How the row's size is measured: the sum of the magnitudes, the length, or the largest.

columns.description: The columns that make up the row, scaled together.

order.by.description: Puts the rows in order by one or more columns, smallest first, for the steps that read the rows before a row.

columns.description: The columns the rows are put in order by: the first decides, each next one decides between rows the ones before call equal.

outliers.clip.description: Holds the extreme values of a column to bounds learned from the training rows.

column.description: The column whose extremes are held.

bounds.description: How the bounds are worked out: by quantile, by spread, or by the middle half.

at.description: How far out the bounds sit: a share for a quantile, nothing for the training extremes; a multiple of the spread or the middle half otherwise.

outlier.description: What happens to a value outside the bounds: held at the edge, made a gap, or refused.

read.csv.description: Reads the rows from a comma-separated file.

path.description: Where the comma-separated file will be, when the pipeline runs.

read.excel.description: Reads the rows from a sheet of an Excel workbook, the first unless one is named, its first row naming the columns.

path.description: Where the workbook will be, when the pipeline runs: .xlsx, .xls or .xlsb.

sheet.description: The sheet the rows are on. Left out, the first sheet.

read.images.description: Reads the rows from a folder of pictures, a folder to a class: a picture a row at the size and channels the step says, the folder it stands in the answer, and a column of nought and one for each class.

path.description: The folder the pictures will be in, when the pipeline runs: a folder to each class, pictures of .png, .jpg, .bmp, .gif or .tga in each.

width.description: How many pixels across every picture is; one that is not is refused, never resized.

height.description: How many pixels down every picture is; one that is not is refused, never resized.

channels.description: How many numbers each pixel is: 1 for grey, 3 for red green blue, 4 with how much shows through.

read.join.description: Reads two comma-separated files as one source: each row of the left file beside the one row of the right file its key names. Rows served later arrive already joined.

oneOf.description: A comma-separated file, read as read.csv reads one: its first line names the columns.

path.description: Where the comma-separated file will be, when the pipeline runs.

left.description: The file whose rows the joined rows are: each of its rows, in its order, beside its partner.

oneOf.description: A comma-separated file, read as read.csv reads one: its first line names the columns.

path.description: Where the comma-separated file will be, when the pipeline runs.

right.description: The file each left row takes its partner from: the one row whose key is the left row's key.

on.description: The columns a left row and its partner share, named alike in both files: each compared as the exact text of its cells, the spaces around it taken off.

unmatched.description: What becomes of a left row whose key the right file does not hold: refuse stops the run, naming the row; drop leaves it out and counts it in the fit.

read.json.description: Reads the rows from a JSON file holding an array of records, one object a row, every value as the file writes it.

path.description: Where the JSON file will be, when the pipeline runs: an array of records, one object a row.

read.parquet.description: Reads the rows from an Apache Parquet file, which says what each of its columns holds.

path.description: Where the Parquet file will be, when the pipeline runs.

read.rows.description: Takes rows that are handed in rather than opened: a table already in memory, a reader over a query.

description.description: What the rows are, for whoever reads the file later.

read.texts.description: Reads the rows from a folder of text files, a folder to a class: a file a row, the folder it stands in the answer, and a column of nought and one for each class.

path.description: The folder the text files will be in, when the pipeline runs: a folder to each class, files of .txt in each.

scale.given.description: Scales a column into a range from bounds you give, above the split, so a feature worked out after it is worked out from scaled columns.

lowest.description: The lowest value the column can hold.

highest.description: The highest value it can hold.

lands.description: Where the scaled values land: between minus one and one, or between nothing and one.

settle.gaps.description: Settles the gaps in a column with a value no row decided, so a feature worked out from it is not a gap.

column.description: The column with gaps in it.

with.description: What goes in the gaps, decided by nobody but you: zero, a constant, or refuse for a column that is not supposed to have gaps at all.

shuffle.description: Puts the rows in an order drawn from a seed, before they are divided, so every part holds the same mixture.

seed.description: The number that makes the shuffle repeatable: the same seed puts the same rows in the same order.

split.atRandom.description: Divides the rows at random, the same way every time for the same seed.

train.description: How the rows are shared out: training, validation, test, a part to predict on and a part to calibrate an interval on, which together make the whole.

validation.description: The share used while choosing between models.

test.description: The share kept back until the end.

predict.description: The share held back to predict on; none when it is left out.

calibration.description: The share an interval is calibrated on, fitted on by nothing and chosen by nothing; none when it is left out.

seed.description: The number that makes the shuffle repeatable: the same seed deals the same rows the same way.

testSeed.description: The number that deals the rows to be measured on, none or more. Given, those rows are the same whatever the seed is, and the seed deals the rest. Left out, the seed deals every part.

folds.description: How many slices the rows that are neither test nor predict are cut into, at least two; one of them is validation and the others are training. Left out, the rows are cut once, as shares say.

fold.description: Which of the slices is validation, counted from nought; said with folds, and below them.

split.byTime.description: Divides the rows by when they happened: the earliest to learn from, the latest to be measured on.

column.description: The column that says when a row happened.

train.description: How the rows are shared out: training, validation, test, a part to predict on and a part to calibrate an interval on, which together make the whole.

validation.description: The share used while choosing between models.

test.description: The share kept back until the end.

predict.description: The share held back to predict on; none when it is left out.

calibration.description: The share an interval is calibrated on, fitted on by nothing and chosen by nothing; none when it is left out.

gap.description: How many of the last moments of every part are kept apart, fitted on by nothing and handed to nothing: at least as many as the rows an answer reads ahead. Left out, none.

origins.description: How many places the cut between training and validation is moved to, at least two; the rows that are neither test nor predict are cut into one block more. Left out, the rows are cut once, as shares say.

origin.description: Which of the places this is, counted from nought; said with origins, and below them.

split.stratified.description: Divides the rows at random while keeping the mixture of one column the same in every part.

column.description: The column whose mixture of values is kept the same in every part.

train.description: How the rows are shared out: training, validation, test, a part to predict on and a part to calibrate an interval on, which together make the whole.

validation.description: The share used while choosing between models.

test.description: The share kept back until the end.

predict.description: The share held back to predict on; none when it is left out.

calibration.description: The share an interval is calibrated on, fitted on by nothing and chosen by nothing; none when it is left out.

seed.description: The number that makes the shuffle repeatable: the same seed deals the same rows the same way.

folds.description: How many slices the rows that are neither test nor predict are cut into, at least two; one of them is validation and the others are training. Left out, the rows are cut once, as shares say.

fold.description: Which of the slices is validation, counted from nought; said with folds, and below them.

target.description: Names the column a model is asked to predict, which is handed over apart from the numbers it is shown.

column.description: The column a model is asked to predict, handed over apart from the numbers it is shown.

target.ahead.description: Names an answer read from a column rows later in the declared order: the value then, or the return on the row's own value by then.

column.description: The column the answer is read from, rows later.

ahead.description: How many rows later the answer is read, in the declared order: at least one.

as.description: What the answer is: the value itself then, or the return on the row's own value by then.

target.distribution.description: Names the columns a model is asked to predict as one answer: how a whole is divided among them, in their order.

columns.description: The columns the answer is divided among, in their order: at least two.

scaleBy.description: The column saying how many the shares are shares of, so predictions come back as how many fell in each; left out, they come back as shares.

ordered.description: Whether the columns are in an order that means something, as bands of weight are, so a prediction is measured by how far its shares lie from the answer's along it; left out, they are not.

remainder.description: The column made for what is left of the whole once the columns are counted, when fewer arrive than the column saying how many there were; left out, the columns hold the whole.

target.labels.description: Names the columns a model is asked to predict as one answer of labels, each nought or one on every row.

columns.description: The columns holding the labels, each nought or one on every row: at least two.

ones.description: How many of the columns hold a one on every row: one when a row is exactly one of its things; left out, any number.

target.numbers.description: Names the columns a model is asked to predict as one answer of free numbers, each any finite number.

columns.description: The columns holding the numbers of the answer, in their order: at least two.

watch.reference.description: Keeps the training rows of the columns it watches, as counts, so rows served later can be measured against them.

warnAbove.description: The distance above which two parts are flagged as unlike: a share above nought, at most one.

columns.description: The columns to keep the training rows of; left out, every column where it stands but the id, the answer and the columns the rows are ordered or divided in time by.
